Subject: Finexa security & procurement next steps (SOC 2 + stakeholder map)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Validate security posture and procurement requirements so your team can complete a technical & commercial review by early March.
- Key decision criteria you mentioned: SOC 2 report, recent pen test/summary, access to audit logs (sample), and data retention + encryption details. Also unit cost + predictable latency for high-volume inference were noted as business priorities.

Can you confirm the internal stakeholders we should be mapping to the procurement process? From the call I captured:
- Economic buyer: Carlos Vega (CFO) — will lead budget/contract approval
- Security reviewer: Meera Shah (Head of Security) — technical/compliance questions
- Procurement: procurement@finexa.com — will drive contract SOW and T&Cs

If that looks right, next steps from our side: we will package SOC2, pen-test summary, and a small sample of audit logs and deliver them to you by EOD Friday (2026-02-14). I’ll loop in Marissa (security SME) to handle the artifacts and Dev for any technical Qs.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync with Meera + Carlos on Tue 2026-02-16 to walk through the artifacts and clarify any outstanding security questions. Are they available then?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. If procurement prefers a DocuSign preview, we can prepare a draft once legal confirms T&Cs.

Hey Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with what I have. A few clarifications:

- Stakeholders: Confirmed
  - Carlos Vega (CFO) — economic buyer, will sign off on spend
  - Meera Shah (Head of Security) — will own the security review
  - procurement@finexa.com — procurement team (lead: Tanya Li) will manage the legal/contract review

- Procurement timeline: Procurement would like SOC 2 and pen-test artifact + answers to a short security questionnaire to start their legal review. Ideally they want materials by 02/16 so they can review before our next legal committee meeting on 03/01. Goal is to complete contract signature by ~03/05 if everything looks good.

- Questions for you:
  1) Can Redwood provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II for 2025, and a one-page pen-test summary (high-level findings + remediation status)?
  2) Sample audit logs: a CSV or text file with anonymized entries is perfect, we only need a representative snapshot.
  3) Short answers on data retention (how long do you keep request logs, KV/prefix cache retention), and encryption (at-rest, in-transit, KMS).

If you can get these to us by EOD 02/14, that would be great. Meera is available for the 02/16 slot at 10:00am PST — Carlos is tentatively available, I’ll confirm with him.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Johnson
Director of Platform Partnerships, Finexa
alice.johnson@finexa.com | +1 (415) 555-0789

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T16:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finexa security & procurement next steps (SOC 2 + stakeholder map)

Hi Alice —

As promised, attaching the initial set of artifacts for your procurement and security review. All attachments are redacted where appropriate. If you need a non-redacted copy we can coordinate an NDA / secure share.

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2_report_2025_v1.pdf (redacted)
- pen_test_summary_2025.pdf
- audit_logs_sample.csv (anonymized entries)

Quick answers to the items you asked about:
- SOC 2: We completed a SOC 2 Type II for 2025. Redacted report attached.
- Pen test: External pentest completed Q3 2025; one-pager attached summarizing scope and remediation status (no critical issues, all high/medium findings remediated).
- Audit logs: Attached is a sampled CSV export with anonymized request IDs, timestamps, and event types.
- Data retention: Request logs retained for 90 days by default; aggregated usage metrics retained 2 years. KV/prefix cache is ephemeral and kept in GPU memory per session; persistent logs are only the ones in the audit export.
- Encryption & keys: All customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. Customer keys can be managed via KMS (we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private).

If Meera or procurement need any additional documentation (e.g., architecture diagram, access to a secure S3 with full logs, or a live walkthrough of logging), let me know and we’ll set that up.

Ben — sending to procurement@finexa.com in parallel now per Alice’s note.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment stubs included: SOC2_report_2025_v1.pdf, pen_test_summary_2025.pdf, audit_logs_sample.csv]
